blocks.text: Global warming refers to the long-term rise in the Earth’s average surface temperature due to human activities, primarily the emission of greenhouse gases (GHGs) released by burning fossil fuels.

blocks.title: Greenhouse effect
blocks.text: The progressive warming up of the earth’s surface due to blanketing effect of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere is called the greenhouse effect.

blocks.text: It is a global scale problem of air pollution. Carbon dioxide and water vapour in the atmosphere transmit short wavelength solar radiations but reflect back the longer wavelength heat radiation coming from warmed surface of the earth.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Greenhouse gases do not reflect infrared radiation. CO₂ and water vapour absorb the longer-wavelength infrared (heat) radiation given off by the warm Earth and re-emit part of it back towards the surface, which keeps the Earth warmer.

The greenhouse effect is a phenomenon which is based on the gases to absorb infra-red radiations. In the day, heat from the sun (in the form of infrared) passes through the atmosphere heating up the earth. At night, the earth radiate heat to the outer space. Some atmospheric gases trap the heat from the sun, thus, preventing the loss of heat. Higher the concentration of carbon dioxide gas and other gases, greater will be the absorption of thermal radiations and greater will be the increase of global temperature.

blocks.prompt: a) Differentiate classical and photochemical smog.
blocks.explanation: Classical (London) smog is a reducing mixture of SO₂, soot and fog from burning coal, formed in cold, damp weather. Photochemical (Los Angeles) smog forms in strong sunlight from reactions of NOₓ and VOCs from traffic; its main components are ozone and PAN (oxidizing), and it is more harmful.

rows: SO₂, soot and fog from burning coal
formed from NOₓ and VOCs from traffic
oxidizing: mainly ozone and PAN; more harmful

blocks.prompt: b) Name greenhouse gases (GHGs). How do these gases cause global warming?
blocks.explanation: Carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, water vapour and CFCs. They let short-wavelength sunlight in, but absorb the long-wavelength infrared heat given off by the Earth and send it back down. The more of these gases there are, the more heat is trapped and the higher the average temperature rises.
